## Book Organization {-}

These notes are organized into six thematic parts plus reference appendices:

1. **Foundations & Preliminaries** — Basic plasma definitions and scales (@sec-intro), mathematical tools (@sec-math), analytical mechanics (@sec-theoretical-mechanics), special relativity (@sec-relativity), and unit systems (@sec-unit).
2. **Single-Particle Dynamics** — Charged-particle drifts and adiabatic invariants (@sec-single) and formal guiding-center theory (@sec-GC).
3. **Fluid & Magnetohydrodynamic Theory** — Two-fluid and MHD equations (@sec-fluid), collisions, diffusion, and resistivity (@sec-resistivity), electron MHD (@sec-emhd), and electromagnetic boundary conditions (@sec-BC).
4. **Waves, Kinetic Theory & Instabilities** — Plasma waves (@sec-waves), kinetic theory and Landau damping (@sec-kinetic), kinetic dispersion relations (@sec-dispersion), fluid and kinetic instabilities (@sec-stability, @sec-kmhd), gyrokinetics (@sec-gyrokinetics), nonlinear phenomena (@sec-nonlinear), and turbulence (@sec-turbulence).
5. **Space & Astrophysical Plasmas** — Magnetic reconnection (@sec-reconnection), collisionless shocks (@sec-shock), the solar wind (@sec-solarwind), magnetospheric physics (@sec-magnetosphere, @sec-flr, @sec-iono, @sec-radiation_belt, @sec-aurora), cosmic-ray transport (@sec-cosmic-ray), and observational geometry/diagnostics (@sec-geometry).
6. **Computational Plasma Physics** — Particle-in-Cell (@sec-pic), hybrid kinetic-fluid methods (@sec-hybrid), ray tracing (@sec-ray-tracing), and standard numerical benchmark tests (@sec-test).
7. **Appendices** — Electromagnetism circuit analogies (@sec-inductance, @sec-capacitance) and a quick-reference plasma physics formulary (@sec-appendix-formulary).
